title: Mechanistic Insights into the Allosteric Regulation of P53 Y220C by Small-Molecule Stabilizers.
authors: Wen, Yiming; Niu, Buying; Meng, Jingyi; Chen, Danye; Li, Xutong; Zhang, Suilin; Agren, Hans; Zheng, Mingyue; Teng, Dan
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
one_liner_zh: 该文通过微秒级分子动力学模拟和残基相互作用网络分析，研究小分子稳定剂对p53 Y220C突变体的变构调控机制，揭示其恢复DNA结合界面和长程协同网络的作用，虽非直接预测TF-DNA结合位点，但聚焦于转录因子p53的DNA结合界面恢复与变构机制，方法可迁移至TF-DNA互作建模。
abstract: The p53 Y220C mutation is a recurrent hotspot alteration that induces local unfolding and long-range functional disruption, compromising its tumor suppressor activity. While small-molecule stabilizers targeting this mutation have shown therapeutic promise, their underlying allosteric regulatory mechanisms remain poorly defined. Here, we investigate two p53 Y220C stabilizers with near-identical scaffolds but over 60-fold difference in activity, serving as a model to dissect the structural basis of differential efficacy. Through microsecond-scale molecular dynamics simulations and residue interaction network analysis, we reveal that the more active compound not only engages the mutation-induced cavity but also restores long-range cooperative networks and DNA-binding interfaces by rewiring key allosteric communication pathways disrupted by the mutation. Our results uncover a multilayered allosteric rescue mechanism involving dynamic pocket engagement, hydrophobic core reconstruction, and intramolecular signal reactivation. These findings move beyond conventional binding-affinity explanations and highlight the importance of network-level conformational regulation in mutant p53 rescue. This work establishes a mechanistic foundation for rational stabilizer design, proposing a new strategy centered on allosteric network restoration and mutation-adaptable anchoring. It offers broader implications for targeting conformationally unstable transcription factors previously considered "undruggable".
abstract_zh: p53 Y220C突变是一种复发性热点改变，诱导局部去折叠和长程功能破坏，损害其肿瘤抑制活性。尽管靶向该突变的小分子稳定剂已显示出治疗前景，但其潜在变构调控机制仍不明确。在此，我们研究两种具有几乎相同骨架但活性差异超过60倍的p53 Y220C稳定剂，将其作为模型来剖析差异效力的结构基础。通过微秒级分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟和残基相互作用网络分析，我们揭示出活性更高的化合物不仅结合突变诱导的空腔，还通过重新连接被突变破坏的关键变构通讯通路，恢复长程协同网络和DNA结合界面。我们的结果揭示了一种多层变构拯救机制，涉及动态口袋结合、疏水核心重建和分子内信号再激活。这些发现超越了传统的结合亲和力解释，强调了网络级构象调控在突变p53拯救中的重要性。本研究为合理稳定剂设计建立了机制基础，提出了一种以变构网络恢复和突变适应性锚定为中心的新策略，并对靶向此前被视为“不可成药”的构象不稳定转录因子提供了更广泛的意义。
